claims.text: The feature comprises five mechanically bounded changes plus diagnostics-and-housekeeping; every touch point named in the research plan exists, is structurally sound, and is amenable to the carve-out shape the PRD describes.
The FR-1 reviewer set is larger than the four PRD-named agents: execute-task-quality-handler should be in scope, and finalize-deliverable-packager is a moderate candidate.
The FR-3 parity rule will produce a false-positive on day one against the mcp-openapi-schema row in ADR-0041 unless the design adopts a deprecation-marker convention.
Five remaining decisions reasonably belong to the per-layer designers: FR-1 scope, FR-2 self-check site, FR-3 deprecation handling, FR-4 sentinel posture, and FR-7 marker tightening.
shared-document-reviewer is located at .claude/agents/shared-document-reviewer.md and is the pipeline's central reviewer, invoked at five doc_type points per ADR-0017.
shared-document-reviewer emits a verdict object plus severity-tagged findings.
shared-document-reviewer is the largest reviewer file in the project at 26.7KB.
review-architecture-auditor is located at .claude/agents/review-architecture-auditor.md and is the Stage 8 auditor.
review-architecture-auditor's verdict enum is {fail, conditional_pass, pass}.
review-architecture-auditor's severity-to-verdict mapping (BLOCKER → fail, MAJOR → conditional_pass, MINOR/INFO → pass) is explicit in its body.
review-cross-artifact-auditor is located at .claude/agents/review-cross-artifact-auditor.md and is the Stage 11 auditor.
review-cross-artifact-auditor's verdict enum is {fail, conditional_pass, pass, hard_capped} plus a SECONDARY convergence verdict in the same payload.
design-claude-code's FR-1 check must decide whether to inspect one or both of review-cross-artifact-auditor's verdicts (primary and convergence).
execute-phase-quality-reviewer is located at .claude/agents/execute-phase-quality-reviewer.md and is the T7-transition per-phase reviewer.
execute-phase-quality-reviewer emits a 5-dimensional verdict per execution-pipeline-design-r1 Blueprint v5 Contract 2: {PASS, NEEDS_RECONCILIATION, BLOCKER} with findings array adjacent.
execute-task-quality-handler is located at .claude/agents/execute-task-quality-handler.md and is a STRONG candidate for FR-1 inclusion.
execute-task-quality-handler emits a {APPROVED, NEEDS_REVISION, STUB_DETECTED, BLOCKER} status enum with a findings array (domain, severity, source_activity, file_path, locator, message).

In execute-task-quality-handler, an APPROVED status alongside a finding with severity: blocker is the exact contradiction US-1 names; excluding this agent leaves the execution-side per-task path open to the failure mode FR-1 is meant to catch.
finalize-deliverable-packager is located at .claude/agents/finalize-deliverable-packager.md and is a MODERATE candidate for FR-1 inclusion.

finalize-deliverable-packager emits its own {PASS, BLOCK, REVIEW} verdict but the findings field is chained, including reviewer_findings passed through from the shared-document-reviewer it invokes with doc_type: DeliverableArchive.
If shared-document-reviewer already passed the FR-1 check at its own invocation, re-checking at finalize-deliverable-packager may be redundant; design-claude-code decides.
synth-critic uses verdicts but per-CLAIM, not per-INVOCATION; recommend excluding it from FR-1 scope.
synth-framer and synth-synthesizer consume verdicts but don't emit a verdict+findings contract pair.
finalize-reconciler emits a convergence verdict but its primary output is a dispatch JSON; the convergence verdict is a downstream summary, not an artifact verdict that can contradict findings.
The recipe-feature-pipeline parent skill is located at .claude/skills/recipe-feature-pipeline/SKILL.md and is 629 lines.
Per ADR-0044 (flatten decision), recipe-feature-pipeline is the actual parent orchestrator.
recipe-feature-pipeline directly dispatches reviewers at 5 invocation points and the 4 execution specialists at the T1/T2/T7/T9 transitions.
The scope_class is currently read at line 350 of recipe-feature-pipeline SKILL.md, inside Stage 12 (Deliverable Packaging).
FR-2's self-check needs scope_class earlier (at the start of dispatch); design-claude-code under U-2 must hoist the read or add a second read site.
Per ADR-0044, the execute-orchestrator advisor at .claude/agents/execute-orchestrator.md is non-invocable.
execute-orchestrator is the canonical 12-substantive-state machine reference (T0..T13); FR-2's self-check does NOT live here.
The single-agent fallback concept the PRD names is not currently a named state in checkpoint.json.

The single-agent fallback is implicit in checkpoint.execution_mode = "parent-driven-workaround" (the historical fallback mode preserved per ADR-0044 for edge-case resumption) and in any future per-stage agent-selection logic.
design-claude-code under U-2 must define the configuration surface FR-2 inspects.
.claude/skills/auditing-mcp/ is a graduated family-coordinator per ADR-0042, with an empty sub-skill family slot reserved.

.claude/skills/auditing-mcp/ hosts 14 Python scripts: audit_mcp.py (coordinator) plus 10 OP-rule scripts (audit_op1..audit_op10) plus 3 utility scripts (check_toxic_combinations.py, scan_mcp_secrets.py, validate_mcp_config.py).
Each OP script follows a uniform contract: one positional argument, JSON findings to stdout, exit 0/1/2 per pass/fail/error.
.mcp.json at the repo root has six servers registered today: actionlint-mcp, context7, exa, gitnexus, serena, terraform-mcp.
All .mcp.json entries pass OP-1, OP-9, OP-10 cleanly (env-block indirection only).
ADR-0041 v1.0.1 is located at adrs/ADR-0041-install-mechanism-hybrid.md.
ADR-0041's per-server install-mechanism taxonomy table at Decision §1.b has seven rows — including mcp-openapi-schema, which is no longer in .mcp.json.
FR-3 lands as audit_op11_*.py by convention.
Severity tokens for FR-3 are already canonical: BLOCKER, MAJOR, MINOR, NIT.
.devcontainer/postCreate.sh is 174 lines and uses set -euo pipefail.
postCreate.sh installs four OSS-local MCP servers today (serena, actionlint-mcp, terraform-mcp, gitnexus) — was 5, dropped to 4 when mcp-openapi-schema was removed.
postCreate.sh uses sentinel-file + binary-on-PATH check for idempotency (the two-check pattern from ADR-0041 Decision item 3).
FR-4's dry-run sits inside install_gitnexus() just before the npm install -g step (lines ~127-150 of postCreate.sh).
.devcontainer/versions.env holds the pin GITNEXUS_TAG=1.6.5.
Five pins are active in versions.env, by convention one line per pin with full upstream rationale in adjacent comments.
.devcontainer/lib/log-mcp-event.sh is the diagnostic-emission helper implementing ADR-0037 event schema and ADR-0039 redaction-at-source, default-fail-closed.
FR-4 should emit an install_complete (with status:ok|failed) — NOT a new event type (NFR-13 compatibility).
No Dockerfile change is required per ADR-0041's no-Dockerfile posture.
.github/workflows/ does not exist; FR-5's workflow is the first in this project.
There is no precedent for runner choice, SHA-pin, permissions, concurrency, path-filter, or claude-cli-install in this codebase.
The KB defaults (security non-negotiables in KB-github-actions-platform/references/security.md) are the only inputs design-cicd has for FR-5.
Issues/devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1-deferrals/register.md is the target for FR-7.

Rows B-1 (CI smoke) and H-4 (GitNexus dry-run) already carry the adoption parenthetical inline at lines 56 and 141 respectively, marked *(ADOPTED 2026-05-25 by pipeline-quickwins-hardening-r1 — see Issues/cross-artifact-divergence-detection-gap/proposal.md)*.
The Why-excluded, Re-examination-trigger, and Forgetting-risk cells for rows B-1 and H-4 are already updated.

FR-7's substantive work appears to be already in place; design-claude-code / design-composer under U-7 confirms the marker text matches the convention exactly and decides packaging (in-archive vs separate housekeeping commit).
Issues/cross-artifact-divergence-detection-gap/proposal.md status is 'adopted' (frontmatter line 5).
Blast radius for shared-document-reviewer (FR-1) is MEDIUM with 2 one-hop dependents (recipe-feature-pipeline at 5 points; packager at 1).
FR-1 is shape-validating, not shape-changing.
Blast radius for review-architecture-auditor (FR-1) is LOW with 2 one-hop dependents (parent orchestrator; finalize-reconciler).
Blast radius for review-cross-artifact-auditor (FR-1) is MEDIUM with 2 one-hop dependents; the two verdicts in the same payload (primary + convergence) need disambiguation.
Blast radius for execute-phase-quality-reviewer (FR-1) is LOW with 2 one-hop dependents (parent orchestrator at T7; execute-finalize-reconciler); well-isolated via Contract 6 dispatch_directives.
Blast radius for recipe-feature-pipeline (FR-2) is HIGH with approximately 25 sub-agent dependents; it is a single dispatch nexus.
Blast radius for auditing-mcp (FR-3) is LOW with 1 one-hop dependent (Gate-6 hard gate per ADR-0043); additive new OP rule with no schema break.
Blast radius for postCreate.sh (FR-4) is MEDIUM; affects every Codespace rebuild; false positive breaks bring-up for every contributor.
Blast radius for .github/workflows/ (FR-5) is LOW for blast / MEDIUM for first-precedent, with no current dependents (greenfield); workflow shape becomes the project's convention.

Blast radius for .mcp.json (FR-3 + FR-5 probed) is MEDIUM with dependents being Claude Code parser plus 7 sub-agents with mcp__ allowlists; read-only and risk is in misinterpretation; NFR-15 specifies no allowlist change.
The HIGH risk on recipe-feature-pipeline is structural (single point of dispatch) rather than indicative of poor design.

The five mechanisms in aggregate touch recipe-feature-pipeline four times (FR-1 check site or hook attachment, FR-2 self-check, FR-3 audit dispatch reads, FR-7 metadata); design-claude-code should ensure the four touches compose cleanly rather than colliding.
Verdict emission convention: always a single string field inside a structured JSON output object; field name is consistently verdict or status.
Findings convention: always a JSON array adjacent to the verdict; finding object shape (severity, file_path, message, rule/domain identifiers) varies by reviewer.
design-claude-code's FR-1 validator must accommodate the variance in finding object shape or extract a common subset.
Severity taxonomy: four canonical tokens — BLOCKER, MAJOR, MINOR, NIT/INFO.
Severity-to-verdict mapping is deterministic: any BLOCKER → fail/BLOCK/BLOCKER; any MAJOR (no BLOCKER) → conditional_pass / NEEDS_RECONCILIATION; only MINOR/INFO → pass.
The canonical blocking-severity that U-1 asks about is BLOCKER (plus the auditor-family alias 'blocker' lowercase used in execute-task-quality-handler's findings).
ONLY design-composer authors ADRs per FR-5; all other agents may cite, not author.
Auditing skills and reviewers are report-only; the 'enforce vs instruct' choice for FR-1/FR-2 must add an enforcing layer ON TOP of these report-only contracts.
Agent frontmatter requires: name, description, model, effort, tools, skills, memory.
Logging convention: TaskUpdate at start and end of sub-agent work (one line each); the parent skill writes checkpoint.json and state-transitions.log.
auditing-mcp rule naming convention: OP-N (integer); FR-3 is OP-11 by convention.
auditing-mcp script naming convention: audit_op<N>_<short-descriptor>.py.
auditing-mcp script contract: one positional argument (path-to-.mcp.json), JSON findings to stdout, exit 0/1/2 (no findings / BLOCKER finding / internal error).
auditing-mcp finding format is {rule, severity, server, field, message}; FR-3 must include {prescribed_form, live_form, diff_dimension} to satisfy AC-FR-3-b.
Each OP rule's rationale lives in references/; FR-3 should add a new section to references/anti-patterns.md or a dedicated reference file.
Shell posture convention: set -euo pipefail at the top of every script.

Two sentinel-naming conventions coexist: ADR-0041 canonical is <server>@<version>.installed under .claude/runtime/install-sentinels/; live in postCreate.sh is .install-sentinel-<server>-<version> directly under .claude/runtime/.
FR-4 must NOT introduce a third sentinel-naming convention.
Idempotency convention is sentinel-presence AND binary-on-PATH (two-check pattern).
The log_mcp_event helper writes one JSONL record per install/probe to .claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl.
Event types per ADR-0037 are install_complete, readiness_probe, structured_failure; FR-4 must use one of these existing types — no new event type (NFR-13).
Diagnostic format is dual stream: single-line [postCreate] <message> to stderr for operators, plus structured JSONL via log_mcp_event for machine readers.
FR-6 actionable diagnostics for FR-4 should follow the dual-stream pattern.
CI/CD is GREENFIELD with no existing convention.

design-cicd's baseline KB security non-negotiables are: SHA-pin third-party actions, least-privilege permissions, no untrusted input interpolation in run:, OIDC over long-lived keys, concurrency on deploy workflows.

Deferral-register row update convention: append *(ADOPTED YYYY-MM-DD by <slug> — see <link>)* inline in the Item-cell; update Why-excluded to 'Now adopted: <summary>'; update Re-examination-trigger to 'Adopted by <slug>.'; update Forgetting-risk to 'Resolved by adoption.'.
The TL;DR and counts in the deferral register are NOT incrementally updated row-by-row (snapshot doc, not a live ledger).
Rows B-1 and H-4 already conform to the deferral-register row update convention; FR-7 verifies and tightens, doesn't author.

The execute-orchestrator agent file is documented as 'advisor; non-invocable per ADR-0044' but still carries an invocable-shaped frontmatter block; if FR-2's self-check enumerates agents rather than invocable agents, it could stumble.
Sentinel-naming inconsistency between ADR-0041 canonical and live postCreate.sh form is minor severity; FR-4 should adopt one of the two existing conventions or be sentinel-less.
postCreate.sh lines 11 and 165 say '5 OSS-local servers' — should be 4 post-2026-05-24 removal; minor severity; cosmetic; not a quick-wins-hardening concern.

Open question U-1 (FR-1 scope completeness): Should execute-task-quality-handler be in FR-1 scope (strong sweep recommendation)? finalize-deliverable-packager? The PRD's named four are illustrative; the intent doc's binding framing is 'any reviewer that emits a verdict+findings pair.'

Open question U-3 (FR-3 deprecation handling): ADR-0041 still lists mcp-openapi-schema as one of seven invocation rows; .mcp.json has six servers; AC-FR-3-c naturally reads as a day-one BLOCKER false-positive.
U-3 option (a): in-rule deprecation marker — preferred by CLAUDE.md framing; respects ADR-0005 append-only.
U-3 option (b): ADR amendment to drop the row — out-of-scope per carve-out.
U-3 option (c): audit-script allowlist of known-deprecated row identifiers — least transparent.
With two existing sentinel conventions, FR-4 likely runs without a sentinel (every rebuild) — but design-codespaces under U-4 confirms.
CLAUDE.md explicitly acknowledges at line 9 that mcp-openapi-schema was removed 2026-05-24 and that KB-mcp-platform still references it as one of seven — 'a stale-doc issue, not an active server.'
The project's posture on stale ADR/KB references is established: removed-from-active-config can coexist with persistent stale references in design-time docs.
FR-3's parity rule should respect the established posture on stale references (in-rule recognition, not forced ADR cleanup).

NFR-13 (MCP event surface compatibility): the existing event types per ADR-0037 are install_complete, readiness_probe, structured_failure; FR-3/4/5 diagnostics must use one of these three or emit no event at all.
Live evidence confirms the MCP event schema is stable: postCreate.sh emits install_complete; postStart.sh emits readiness_probe and structured_failure.

NFR-15 (allowlist preservation): seven sub-agents currently carry mcp__* allowlist entries per ADR-0040: review-architecture-auditor, discovery-external-researcher, discovery-codebase-researcher, design-iac, design-codespaces, design-claude-code, design-cicd.
This feature's mechanisms do not add new MCP servers or change which sub-agents need MCP access; NFR-15 is satisfied by construction.
The GitNexus tag currently pinned in `.devcontainer/versions.env` line 36 is `GITNEXUS_TAG=1.6.5`, corresponding to npm `gitnexus@1.6.5` and GitHub tag `v1.6.5` on `abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus`.
claims.notes: Cited as `.devcontainer/versions.env` line 36 in the research note.

claims.text: At `gitnexus@1.6.5`, the env-var contract is implemented by two explicit early-exit guards in the package's `postinstall` hook — `scripts/build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs` and `scripts/build-tree-sitter-proto.cjs`.
Both postinstall guard scripts perform a strict `=== '1'` string comparison against `process.env.GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS`.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs line 9 and build-tree-sitter-proto.cjs lines 28-34 at v1.6.5.

claims.text: On a strict-string match, the guard scripts `process.exit(0)` after a stable, prefixed warning to stderr.
At tag `v1.6.5`, the `gitnexus/` package's `postinstall` hook is defined in `package.json` as `node scripts/build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs && node scripts/build-tree-sitter-proto.cjs`.
`scripts/build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs` at v1.6.5 checks `process.env.GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS === '1'` at line 9.

On match, `scripts/build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs` prints `[tree-sitter-dart] Skipping build (GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1). Dart parsing will be unavailable until reinstalled without the env var.` to stderr and `process.exit(0)` at line 13.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs lines 5-14 at v1.6.5.

claims.text: A comment at line 7 of `build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs` reads: "Strict `=== '1'` only — '=true', '=yes', '=0' (read as a string)".
claims.notes: Verbatim quote (≤15 words) from build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs comment line 7 at v1.6.5.

claims.text: The proto builder duplicates the strict `=== '1'` check at lines 28-34, prints `[tree-sitter-proto] Skipping build (GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1). Proto parsing will be unavailable until reinstalled without the env var.` and exits 0.
The two postinstall guard scripts run sequentially via `&&` chaining in the `postinstall` line, so either script's failure or skip is independent of the other.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: package.json postinstall field at v1.6.5.

claims.text: When the env-var is not set (or is set to any non-`'1'` value), `build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs` reaches line 39 and executes `execSync('npx node-gyp rebuild', { cwd: dartDir, stdio: 'pipe', timeout: 180000 })`.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs line 39 at v1.6.5.

claims.text: `build-tree-sitter-proto.cjs` invokes the equivalent `npx node-gyp rebuild` call at line 68.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: build-tree-sitter-proto.cjs line 68 at v1.6.5.

claims.text: `node-gyp rebuild` is the C++-toolchain entry point that fans out to `python3`, `make`, and `g++` (or platform equivalents).
The literal binaries `node-gyp` dispatches to (`cc`, `g++`, `make`, `python3`) depend on the host platform.
Absence of `node-gyp` in the process tree is itself a strong positive signal that the env-var guard tripped.
`gitnexus@1.6.5`'s `package.json` lists `tree-sitter-dart`, `tree-sitter-kotlin`, `tree-sitter-proto`, and `tree-sitter-swift` under `optionalDependencies`.
The `postinstall` script in `package.json` at v1.6.5 only references the dart and proto builders — there is no `build-tree-sitter-swift.cjs` invocation in the hook line.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: package.json scripts field at v1.6.5.

claims.text: The README's "Faster install" section states the env-var skips Dart/Proto/Swift grammars.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: README at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/main/README.md (Environment variables section).

claims.text: At v1.6.5, Swift's build outcome is independent of `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS`: npm's intrinsic behavior for `optionalDependencies` is to tolerate prebuild/install failures silently, so `tree-sitter-swift`'s build will already proceed to failure-tolerated-skip on a host without a working C++ toolchain regardless of the env var.
claims.notes: Non-obvious calibration finding F-4; Swift is NOT actually gated by the env-var at v1.6.5.

claims.text: Upstream issue #1024, opened 2026-04-22 by user `zenprocess` and closed not-planned, documents that `tree-sitter-swift@0.6.0`'s `binding.gyp` is malformed and never compiles successfully.
The in-tree workaround `scripts/patch-tree-sitter-swift.cjs` is referenced in issue #1024 but is NOT invoked by the v1.6.5 postinstall hook.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: issue #1024 cross-referenced with package.json postinstall field at v1.6.5.

claims.text: The README and the actual postinstall hook diverge on Swift: the README claims the env var skips Swift; the code claims it skips Dart + Proto.

A dry-run that asserts "Swift was not built because GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1" would be technically false even though Swift typically is unbuilt for the unrelated reason that its binding.gyp is malformed.

When the dart guard trips, the path `<global node_modules root>/gitnexus/node_modules/tree-sitter-dart/build/Release/tree_sitter_dart_binding.node` is never created because `node-gyp rebuild` never runs.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs line 17 (path construction) at v1.6.5.

claims.text: The dart script computes the artifact path `tree_sitter_dart_binding.node` at line 17.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: build-tree-sitter-dart.cjs line 17 at v1.6.5.

claims.text: The proto equivalent artifact path is `<global node_modules root>/gitnexus/node_modules/tree-sitter-proto/build/Release/tree_sitter_proto_binding.node`.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: symmetric path in build-tree-sitter-proto.cjs at v1.6.5.

claims.text: The literal path under `<global node_modules root>` depends on the npm prefix (e.g., `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/...` vs `~/.nvm/versions/node/<v>/lib/node_modules/...`), so a dry-run must derive the location from `npm root -g` rather than hard-coding.
claims.notes: F-5 caveat — operational guidance for dry-run implementation.

claims.text: The README explicitly frames the env-var as a toolchain-abstinence flag, not merely a speedup.
claims.notes: Upstream citation: README at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/main/README.md, Quick Start and Environment variables sections.

claims.text: Skipping the Dart and Proto rebuilds eliminates the only places `gitnexus@1.6.5`'s postinstall would invoke `node-gyp rebuild`, which is the entry point that transitively requires `python3`, `make`, and `g++`.
The README states: "set `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1` … skip vendored grammar materialize/build".
claims.notes: Verbatim quote (≤15 words) from README Quick Start section.

claims.text: The CHANGELOG entry for v1.6.5 covers Docker-runtime image, ca-certificates, and duckdb installer; env-var gating is not new in this release and is therefore not re-mentioned.
The env-var's contract has been stable since prior tags before v1.6.5.
claims.notes: F-6 caveat; supported by absence of CHANGELOG mention at v1.6.5.

claims.text: Observable signal 1 — Stderr signal (positive): each builder emits a prefixed warning containing the literal substring `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1`; the prefixes `[tree-sitter-dart]` and `[tree-sitter-proto]` are stable, and asserting both prefixes appear is a positive, idempotent test.

Observable signal 2 — Process-tree signal (negative-as-positive): `node-gyp` is never invoked, and a dry-run can capture the process tree (e.g., via `strace -f -e trace=execve` or by polling `pgrep`) and assert no descendant of the `npm install` process has argv starting with `node-gyp` or descends to `cc1plus` / `g++`.
claims.notes: Synthesis section signal (2); defensible only when paired with signals 1 and 3.

claims.text: Observable signal 3 — Artifact-absence signal (positive): after install, `npm root -g`/`gitnexus/node_modules/tree-sitter-dart/build/Release/tree_sitter_dart_binding.node` does NOT exist (same for the proto path), which is positive because the dry-run asserts a known path is absent rather than asserting "no error occurred."

Observable signal 4 — Wall-clock signal (positive, weak): the install completes in seconds rather than minutes, useful as a sanity check but not load-bearing because future versions might cache prebuilt `.node` files or add unrelated slow steps.
claims.notes: Synthesis section signal (4); analyst recommends NOT making this the only positive assertion.

claims.text: Recommended dry-run combination (strongest pair): assert (1) prefix appears in stderr AND (3) artifact path is absent; (1) alone is too literal-string-fragile across upstream changes, while (3) alone could be true for other reasons (e.g., the optional dep itself was rejected by npm).
claims.notes: Synthesis section recommended positive-assertion pair; both together pin down that the guard ran AND prevented the artifact.

claims.text: The dry-run should NOT assert anything about Swift via this env-var; the README is misleading at v1.6.5 because script-level reality only covers Dart and Proto.

If Swift coverage matters to the dry-run, treat it as a separate observation: "tree-sitter-swift's binding.gyp is malformed at the pinned tag; its build is failure-tolerated by npm regardless of env-var state per upstream issue #1024."
claims.notes: Analyst guidance from Synthesis section; cross-references issue #1024.

claims.text: Drift mode DM-1 (most likely): upstream factors the env-var check into a shared helper or shifts the literal warning text, so dry-runs that pattern-match on the full sentence break, but those that pattern-match on the env-var name + a "Skipping" verb still pass.
claims.notes: AC-3 drift mode DM-1; mitigation: regex on `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS.*[Ss]kip` rather than the full literal.

claims.text: Drift mode DM-2 (medium likelihood): upstream adds a third optional grammar (e.g., Kotlin, currently in `optionalDependencies` but with no postinstall builder) and forgets to gate it on the env var; the contract silently degrades, with env-var honored for Dart/Proto but a new grammar building anyway.
claims.notes: AC-3 drift mode DM-2; mitigation: enumerate the postinstall script set at install time and warn if it grows.

claims.text: Drift mode DM-3 (medium likelihood, drift toward removal): upstream removes `tree-sitter-dart` or `tree-sitter-proto` entirely (per the same pattern as issue #1024's Swift removal proposal); the builder script vanishes and the env-var becomes silently meaningless.
claims.notes: AC-3 drift mode DM-3; mitigation: assert at least one of the two known scripts exists at the pinned tag before invoking install.

claims.text: Drift mode DM-4 (low likelihood, latent): upstream loosens the comparison from `=== '1'` to truthy-checking; currently anything other than literal `'1'` falls through to rebuild, but if loosened, `=true` etc. would skip — not destructive to the dry-run's positive assertions but changes the contract's edge behavior.
claims.notes: AC-3 drift mode DM-4; mitigation: set the env-var to `0` AND verify the artifact IS built, as a calibration step.
